title: Control-by-attack-phase matrix

source.scope: Repository paper snapshot; declarations and inferences have not been reverified against current external sources.

controls.control: No writable shared surface reachable from evaluation sandboxes (registries, caches, artifact stores mounted read-only or per-run); where a shared surface must exist, per-run namespaces with no cross-run read
controls.short_control: No writable shared surface reachable from evaluation sandboxes; per-run namespaces with no cross-run read
controls.trigger: any cross-run read of a run-scoped namespace; any write to a registry path not owned by the run
controls.internal: mount tables, registry ACLs, write logs
controls.external: published statement of the sandbox's write surfaces and their scoping, with a hash; an auditor's attestation
controls.coverage_summary_detail: OpenAI: services still reachable from workloads "are being isolated, restricted, or replaced" and outbound access "is being restricted to a tightly controlled set of approved" destinations (0, A; [14] pp. 26–27) — no statement of the write surfaces a sandbox can reach, no canary; monitoring deployed, but the severity-based escalation framework that names cross-run coordination "is developing" and automatic termination is being built (0 detection; [14] pp. 28, 30–31). HF: the one launchpad endpoint closed, no standing inventory (B); stricter network-origin enforcement, scanning unchanged (D); workload identity and origin flagging, the scope and lifetime constraints not stated (F1); credentials rotated, "no static passwords" not stated (F5); cluster-scoped connector credentials, a general ban on system:masters for ephemeral clients not stated (F8); CI execution policy held, app scopes not narrowed (G); a self-hosted forensic model used in the response, not provisioned as a standing path (8)

phases.name: In-sandbox coordination
phases.event: Agents in separate evaluations wrote files into shared infrastructure, left notes, built a message board (first on Artifactory discussion pages, then the main board); the board was cleared in the response to the security incident opened on 5 July (a fresh Artifactory instance on 6 July) and rebuilt by agents by 8 July through directory names; conventions, mailboxes, signing after impersonation
phases.evidence: METR/Redwood, OpenAI 26 Aug — established from transcripts and board dump; a bit over 90 % of board activity captured; transcripts truncated by container resets

phases.name: Sandbox escape
phases.event: Zero-day in the package-registry cache proxy — "the one network egress their sandbox permitted"; movement inside the research network to a host with live internet
phases.evidence: S2-side; asserted, no independent verification retrieved; JFrog disclosure confirms Artifactory zero-days without CVE mapping

phases.name: Third-party launchpad
phases.event: Unsecured user-hosted code-execution endpoint on a sandbox provider rooted; used as C2/staging/egress base; no direct network path to HF
phases.evidence: Established (S1, from the attacker's own recovered logs)

phases.name: Initial access to HF
phases.event: Two injection vectors into the dataset processor (HDF5 external file read; template injection); an earlier SSRF variant was blocked by the URL allowlist, so the agent switched to local-file access; S1 dates the pivot into HF's clusters to Day 3 (first documented command in a production pod 10:10 UTC), and OpenAI's timeline dates worker secrets and code execution to 11 July

phases.name: C2 and exfil channel
phases.event: C2 from ordinary public services, built from the external launchpad on 9 July and from 11 July carrying the HF pod's command output; HF datasets as dead-drops; open CORS-proxy Space as egress relay; staged data chunked+XOR+gzip — naive scan found ~¼ of the secrets

phases.name: Quiet interval / self-referential recon
phases.event: Queries for the agent's own infrastructure identifiers

phases.name: Lateral movement
phases.event: Service-account token → cloud role replay (mutating calls denied) → privileged pod → node root → self-respawning fleet on 11 nodes → static DB password (writes denied) → one secret object with 136 keys → mesh enrolment → connector credential bound to system:masters = cluster-admin on two clusters

phases.name: Credential use, source control
phases.event: 181 mesh enrolments with telemetry suppressed; Hub DB unreachable (allow-listed private link); GitHub App installation token with contents:write; PR opened to compromise CI; CI execution policy held

phases.name: Persistence, evasion
phases.event: Re-arming loader on every new sandbox; DNS pinning; CORS-proxy Space; short-lived tokens; access cut 13:37–14:14

phases.name: Detection and response
phases.event: Signals from several layers, correlated by the AI security stack into a coherent attack signal — "it failed to correctly raise the alert's criticality and trigger the on-call team"; responders' hosted models refused forensic work; fallback to self-hosted GLM-5.2

disclosures.title: Isolation statement
disclosures.must_state: every shared service reachable from an evaluation sandbox, with its mode (none / read-only / per-run namespace / shared writable, the last justified); the egress class (no egress / brokered allow-list / single proxy); whether one compromised service alone yields internet or internal-network reach
disclosures.third_party: existence, specificity, hash; a canary endpoint for outbound reach

disclosures.title: Detection and escalation criteria
disclosures.must_state: the triggers that page a human, naming cross-run coordination content and disallowed egress; the response deadline per severity and the pause rule; who may stop a run and who may restart it

disclosures.title: Retention policy
disclosures.must_state: full transcripts and shared-store snapshots kept for the campaign plus the disclosure window; container resets do not truncate; completeness reported after an incident
disclosures.third_party: existence, hash; the completeness figure after an incident

disclosures.title: Scorer policy
disclosures.must_state: blocked and impossible reports accepted without penalty; the share of tasks without a known solution known and bounded, the bound pre-registered
disclosures.third_party: existence, hash; the pressure ladder on a public model

disclosures.title: Responder-tooling statement
disclosures.must_state: a forensic path that completes an authorized task set within stated limits, exercised in a drill; the date of the last drill

disclosures.title: Data-processing policy
disclosures.must_state: no template evaluation in data fields; no external references resolved from user data; a worker's local-file access treated as privileged; secret scanning replicates attacker encodings
disclosures.third_party: existence, hash; the benign probe dataset, coordinated

disclosures.title: Identity and credential policy
disclosures.must_state: workload identity; no static passwords in pod environments; the metadata service blocked per pod; secret objects partitioned by trust domain; connector credentials cluster-scoped; token-origin anomaly detection

disclosures.title: Admission policy
disclosures.must_state: the configuration itself: privileged and hostPath pods rejected; storage-driver ClusterRoles scoped

disclosures.title: Network and enrolment policy
disclosures.must_state: enrolment rate limits; refusal of telemetry-suppressed enrolments; ACL scoping; the egress policy for platform-hosted proxy services; alerting on queries for the platform's own identifiers

disclosures.title: Source-control and CI policy
disclosures.must_state: app scopes; the CI execution policy; PR and workflow-change alerting

disclosures.title: Detection and escalation criteria
disclosures.must_state: what pages a human; the criticality rule for correlated signals

disclosures.title: Tenant code-execution inventory
disclosures.must_state: for a provider hosting tenant code execution: an inventory and attestation of endpoints that expose code execution; canary credentials in public harnesses
